title: Mustard must be installable into a client repository without leaving any versioned trace: nothing it writes — at the root or in any subproject — may appear in that repo's git

waves.summary: Teach the install engine a private mode: a clone-local exclude writer, local-layer settings, and a report that names already-tracked residue.
Make the runtime honour the mode: Guards to the local instruction file, the --private flag on the bootstrap door, and autodetection so the flag is needed once.
Give the installer face the same one-time choice: mustard init --private, and no .github/ scaffolding in a repository that is not the operator's.
Ask real git the whole question: a host repo that already versions its own CLAUDE.md must stay byte-identical and report nothing after a private install, a scan and a spec.
